title: Probing Antialtermagnetism via Orbital-Field-Induced Spin Splitting
abstract: Layer compensation can conceal spin polarization behind a spin-degenerate bulk spectrum in antialtermagnets, preventing spectroscopic identification of the underlying magnetic order. Here we show that the orbital effect of an in-plane magnetic field converts the hidden spin texture into an observable spin splitting of opposite momentum parity, thereby restoring spectroscopic access. Once the parity of the hidden exchange order is determined, complementary response functions in the weak-field regime further resolve its wave character: within a minimal model, we illustrate that a band sum rule over the induced band splittings isolates the momentum gradient of the form factor and differentiates hidden even-parity orders, whereas for odd-parity sectors the induced net spin polarization exhibits characteristic field-amplitude and angular dependences. These results establish orbital-field-induced spin splitting as a generic route to identifying the hidden altermagnetic order parameter without layer resolution.
summary: This theoretical work details a method to overcome spectroscopic limitations in Antialtermagnets by using an in-plane orbital magnetic field. This field induces a spin splitting whose parity is opposite to the hidden magnetic order's parity, allowing researchers to spectroscopically determine the hidden order's wave character. The analysis relies on symmetry principles and momentum-space sum rules.
main_problem: The primary challenge is spectroscopically identifying the hidden magnetic order parameter (and its parity/wave character) in Antialtermagnets (AAMs) when conventional bulk spectroscopy fails due to layer compensation.
main_result: Applying an in-plane orbital magnetic field induces a spin splitting whose parity is opposite to the hidden order parameter's parity, providing a generic spectroscopic route to characterize the hidden order.
method: The analysis uses theoretical modeling involving field-dressed Hamiltonians and deriving symmetry constraints on the induced spin splitting ($\Delta_m(k; B)$) and net spin polarization ($S^\perp$).
model_or_system: The study focuses on a bilayer or multilayer system modeled as an AAM, characterized by a zero-field Hamiltonian exhibiting spin degeneracy due to center-exchange symmetry. The magnetic order parameter's parity ($\chi$) is central to the analysis.
key_observables: Induced spin splitting ($\Delta_m(k; B)$), net spin polarization ($S^\perp(B_\parallel)$), and the momentum dependence of the form factor $f_\alpha(\mathbf{k})$ derived from band sum rules.
important_parameters: In-plane magnetic field strength ($B$), layer number ($L=2N$), and the parity ($\chi$) of the hidden exchange order.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes spin-orbit coupling is weak compared to the nonrelativistic exchange order, and that the orbital contribution can be separated from the Zeeman effect.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the parity conversion (even-parity order $ightarrow$ odd splitting, and vice versa) and show the field dependence of the splitting and polarization for different wave symmetries ($s, d, p$).
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first establishing the spectral degeneracy, then introducing the orbital field to break this degeneracy, and finally using parity theorems, band sum rules, and weak-field expansions to distinguish between different types of hidden magnetic order.
why_interesting: The technique of using orbital fields to probe hidden symmetries and order parameters is highly relevant to understanding complex magnetic ground states in correlated materials, providing a theoretical blueprint for advanced spectroscopic measurements.
